summary: Full backend + frontend E2E test of the multi-brand kitchen sales/recipe/inventory app. Backend: 79/79 pytest tests pass (auth+RBAC, masters CRUD, procurement receipt->approval->stock, intent->issue->production yield, transfer/adjustment/wastage/R&D, recipes versioning, sales draft->post->shortage, daily closing/variance/lock/reopen, 9 reports, dashboard, users admin). Frontend: verified login (valid/invalid), logout, dashboard KPIs+charts+alerts from DB, role-based sidebar for admin/chef/keeper/manager/management, Masters CRUD (brand create+edit, supplier, item, location), settings company name -> sidebar, audit logs, user create, procurement (mandatory invoice validation, upload PNG, pending list, approval dialog with invoice view, approve full -> stock), inventory 6 tabs + ledger filters + adjustment + transfer, kitchen intent -> full issue -> production batch (8KG from 10KG raw), daily closing sheet with expected/physical/variance -> approve & lock (locked badge), sales draft (sold/cancelled/complimentary) + duplicate block + theoretical table + post + insufficient-stock shortage dialog, wastage, R&D trial, recipes page, all 8 reports with CSV export button, mobile hamburger menu. Only one real functional defect found (silent no-op on override for non-privileged roles) plus 3 minor issues.

minor.issue: Accepts empty/blank company_name (no validation) -> sidebar branding renders blank. Add min-length validation.
Reopening a locked day reverts status to 'submitted' but keeps approved_by populated, so Closing History shows 'Approved By: Manoj StoreManager' next to a Submitted badge.

Playbook deviation: no httpOnly cookie is set on login (token returned in JSON for localStorage/Bearer, matching documented design) and CORS uses allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=False. If cookie auth is expected, set httpOnly cookie + explicit origins. Also db.login_attempts grows unbounded (no TTL index).

ui_bugs.issue: Override UI is shown to roles that cannot override. Chef sees 'Override & Post Anyway' + reason field; clicking it silently does nothing (backend returns 200 {ok:false, needs_override:false} and postSale() just re-sets shortages and returns without any toast). No feedback at all, user can click forever. Hide/disable override button when needs_override===false and show toast.error('Only Admin/Store Manager can override').
Sonner toasts render over the top-right user name/logout block, visually clipping 'Chef Chandru / Chef' while a toast is visible. Consider offsetting toaster below the header.

integration_issues.issue: Backend 200 {ok:false, needs_override:false} response is swallowed by postSale(); no error state surfaced in UI

issues: Company name input renders empty until GET /settings resolves (no skeleton/loading state); a fast user (or automation) can save over the blank value and wipe the company name
'Approved By' column populated for rows whose status is Submitted (post-reopen), confusing status display

action_items: Sales.jsx: hide/disable override button + reason input when res.data.needs_override === false, and always show a toast when ok===false (currently a silent dead-click for chef/other roles)
Backend: validate non-empty company_name in PUT /api/settings
Backend: clear approved_by/approved_at when a day is reopened so Closing History status is consistent
Optional: add loading/disabled state to Settings form until GET /settings resolves; add TTL index on login_attempts
critical_code_review_comments: routers_sales.post: returning HTTP 200 with {ok:false} for a business failure forces every client to branch on the body; frontend already mishandles the needs_override=false branch. Prefer 409 with structured detail or make the UI handle all three outcomes explicitly.

Kitchen.jsx issueFull uses `l.qty - (l.issued || 0)` but the intent line payload exposes issued_base (not `issued`), so partial-then-full issue would resend the full requested qty; backend balance check catches it with a 400 but the UI message is confusing.

AuthContext refetches /settings only when user changes; Admin.saveSettings pushes response into context which works, but Admin.load() can overwrite an in-progress edit of the settings form (race observed in testing).
server.py CORS: allow_origins=['*'] is wide open; restrict to the deployed frontend origin.

success_rate.frontend: ~95% (all flows pass; 1 functional UI defect: silent override no-op)

rca_of_the_issue: Silent override no-op: POST /api/sales/{id}/post returns HTTP 200 with {ok:false, shortages:[...], needs_override:<role can override>}. Sales.jsx postSale() checks `if (res.data.needs_override !== undefined && !res.data.ok)` and simply re-renders the shortage dialog, so for a chef (needs_override:false) the second click produces the identical response and no user-visible change or message. The dialog also renders the override button/reason for every role even though the backend only honours override for admin/store_manager (routers_sales.py:146-153). Reproduce: login chef@kitchen.com -> Sales -> Drafts -> Post SALE-00011 -> shortage dialog -> enter reason -> click Override & Post Anyway -> nothing happens (no toast, no network error).
